reviews.comment: Lectures are boring, but his exams are super easy. Didn't learn a whole lot in class as he can be a bit hard to hear sometimes (especially if you sit in the back).

He doesn't give out too much homework and you can learn almost everything from home, however his lectures are great as well as he'll explain both in terms of pure math and conceptually. Tests are also quite easy as he lets you select 7/8 out of 11 problems to complete.

Dr. Battle is a very caring professor. He explains the content at a pace that is easy to follow and writes everything out on the whiteboard. His exams are just like the reviews (8 questions, and you choose 5 to be graded). He emails the assignments out a week in advance, but doesn't really use Canvas.

Good teacher, clearly knows what he is doing. However, I can't say I was fond of the fact that all assignments were emailed out to us and had to be turned in by paper. But, to each their own. Exams are just like the reviews.

He's a decent lecturer and exams are exactly like the reviews so it's not too difficult to do well. His main problems are that he doesn't use canvas and he makes a lot of mistakes but he usually corrects them.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not tech savvy, everything is on the whiteboard. His exams are the only ones significantly different from other profs' exams which makes it hard to know what to expect. Not a horrible choice but I'd look for someone else.

Does not use Canvas so it's hard to tell what your grade is / where you stand in the class. Disliked method of teaching - all on chalkboard and I feel like he could do better at bridging the theory we are learning to the calc we know. I was very lost and the textbook was like hieroglyphics to me. Helpful in office but I could never reach by email.

Very old school - homeworks and exams were given by email. For homeworks, let us work in groups and turn in assignments together. Exams were a little difficult, but they were take home exams so it was expected. With the difficulty of the course content, he made it a lot easier to do well and I still feel like I understand most of the content.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: When I was in the course, we did homework in groups of 3. The weekly homework wasn't too difficult, just be sure to reference the text. He doesn't go through topology which is used in 446 and other courses requiring 409. If you have to take a course with 409 as a perquisite i would look into another professor. Otherwise you'll enjoy him.

He teaches well but is very old-school and rarely uses technology - he had no online content. His exams are also slightly different from (and harder than) all the other profs'. However, your prof doesn't matter much for this class since you can learn everything from Professor Leonard on Youtube. Getting an A is very doable if you study.
Really chill guy. Coming into the class with a C for the prerequisite, managed to get an A with some effort. Take home exams and final. Not mandatory to go to class, just submit it sometimes.

The whole grade is determined by homework and three exams. Professor Battle is not tech-savvy and does not even use Canvas. Exams can be difficult, but if you go to office hours, he tells you exactly how to do the problems. All material is taught by being written out on a chalkboard so make sure to get the notes written
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very disorganized class. Will spend lecture writing proofs. Went to every lecture but still had to teach myself the entire course. He literally hand writes his exams so they are different than any practice exam that is given from other profs, and the last two exams are very hard, after somewhat easy first two exams.  I would not take him again.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Guy Battle had a teaching style that I personally did not like, basing the lecture more on theory and definitions over the topic whilst giving a scarce amount of mathematical examples. Using the homeworks and week-in-reviews will assure you atleast a B. Also curves the class in the end

Grade is 20% hw & take home quiz (easy if you don't procrastinate), and 4x20% exams (partial credit in frq) which the first two is easy and last two is hard.
His lecture is somewhat disorganized, but office hour is very helpful, you gotta self-study lots to completely understand the material.
Overall entire course is not bad if you put the work in.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Battle is one of the best professors I ever had. Even though his lectures can be bit confusing and disorganized, he is willing to help you during his office hours. He doesn't prefaces the topic he will be teaching. His practice exams can be deceiving at sometimes. But he gives a lot of partial credits and curves the final exam.

Not the best lecturer because he uses a lot of Mathematical jargon but I barely went to lectures in the last 6 weeks and still got an A with GOOD margins. WATCH PROFESSOR LEONARD on YouTube. He is the absolute GOAT. And when you take a Quiz or Test, always go to Dr. Battle's office hours to bargain for more points, I once went from an 86 to a 93.

Love the professor. He is an amazing professor. The only thing was is the final. Every other exam was similar to the reviews given. But make sure that you review more than just what the review gives, for the final. Oh and do the homework. Every homework, any homework. Quizzes are take home and easy.

His lectures can be quite confusing, and he is unprepared with his examples, which are often confusing. I had to self learn some more difficult topics. 

Despite this, Prof. Battle clearly knows what he is doing, and his teaching is quite good in most lectures. TAKE ADVANTAGE OF HIS OFFICE HOURS; he is very helpful one on one.

He tends to use different notations in lectures, he does not post any resources on Canvas but sends them through email instead, and there are no outline notes provided. His exams are much harder but he does curve the class. This makes attending class mandatory. He handwrites all his quizzes and exams, making them hard to read and prone to mistakes.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Battle is a big fan of pen and paper, which in my opinion is perfect for math, especially Calc 3. His lectures are confusing until you do the homework, so don't fall behind on those.

Guy Battle is a great prof to take for 251.  His lectures aren't always the most interesting, but he clearly knows what he's talking about. He grades very leniently and the quizzes/exams that he writes are significantly easier than the exams given by other profs.  He cares about his students a lot and is always willing to give points back on exams.

He knows his stuff, but is not organized. He does not set up a canvas page, and you never get solutions or feedback of what you are doing wrong. His lectures are boring and confusing. That being said, the exams are very similar to the homework problems

Dr. Battle is a good choice for 401. Lectures can get really nasty, but if you go to office hours he'll make sure you understand the material. Exams are very similar to the review problems. Homework is long but it's done in groups of 3. Remember to keep track of your grade cause he does everything on paper and email (no Canvas), so dont skip often.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Battle is cool. He was really clear with expectations and gave test reviews that were very similar to the test and he curves a lot. He was always accessible outside of his normal office hours and was genuinely so kind. He is a little unorthadox, he allegedly once faxed his students from Home Depot. But he loves teaching. 12/10 would take again.

GOAT. His lectures could get very confusing, but if you go to his office hours, he will explain better and make it make sense. there was only 4 grades: HW(done in groups of 2-3), E1, E2, E3(not a final just another exam). most importantly, ALWAYS TALK TO HIM ABOUT EXAM GRADES AFTER THEY ARE GRADED. He is very nice and gives a ton of points back!
Wonderful, passionate professor. Problems are clear, probability as a class is enjoyable, proofs are understandable and neat. Expectations for exams are crystal clear.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Battle really knows his stuff. Extremely smart. Very sweet person and is always willing to help you. Sometimes you can get lost during lectures but if you show up to office hours he will make sure you know exactly how to do the homework. Exams are just like the homework. Extremely fair grader and is a really fun person to talk to. Very good.

Dry lectures without preface can be hard to follow, but theories can be suprisingly intuitive. Quizzes are take home, homework has lowest 3 dropped. What's expected on the test is made very clear. Very bright professor, highly recommend for any 200 class or higher. Online resources such as Professor Leonard on YT make this class a breeze.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice guy. Lectures are focused primarily on proofs which gets tedious at times. Generous grader and is eager to help you out if needed. Office hours & reviewing his practice exams before his tests are the way.

Dr. Battle is super nice, but he never prefaces a topic before starting lecture so it can be hard to follow at times. He also lectures in a different order than the homework so most of the time you'll be doing homework on topics not covered yet. His quizzes are set up super similar to exams tho. He also doesn't post anything online so take notes
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Battle was an excellent prof who designed the class well. In order of difficulty we were assigned: Practice Exams, weekly homeworks and (Take-home-open-internet) Quizzes, and Tests. Dr. Battle was very patient in answering questions. He doesn't assign the textbook, but second to his practice exams it was very helpful review resource.

Probably a solid choice for 251 if youre actually trying to get an A and understand why the formulas work the way they do (spends a lot of time on proofs). Only thing would be that the proofs get boring, but I enjoyed understanding the formulas rather than doing a bunch of practice problems. Pretty good choice, but the lectures can get boring.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures were proof-heavy and could be confusing at times. Dr. Battle provides reviews for tests but not answers. If you go into office hours he will work them through. Know how to do the reviews and you'll do well on the tests. Sometimes lecture topics were ahead of the topics in WebAssign for the week, but it wasn't too bad. Very nice guy overall

Really appreciated Dr. Battle's lectures, they were helpful as he is the one creating the exams from scratch. However, there are no formula sheets or good review resources for the exams. I was kind of jealous of other professor's review materials. Definitely not the worst professor, but not the best either. Attend lectures so you don't get lost.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures--Graded by few things--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Not bad overall. The lectures are pretty dry, but the examples help a lot with weekly quizzes and exams. If you go to his office hours, he helps you with the review, which is basically the exam with different numbers. The webassign sometimes isn't related to lecture topics which can be a bit frustrating. One of the easier math profs in my opinion.

Weekly Quizzes that are super helpful for the Exam and weekly homework that is sometimes unrelated to the exam. Lectures are pretty boring and he goes over proofs a lot but the tests are very easy. He gives past exams but not the answers. He's very old fashioned and only uses email.

Grade consists of weekly homework assignments, 2 midterms, and a final. Lectures are pretty boring. Homework questions come from the book (which you can find online for free) and are pretty easy. Exams are a bit more difficult but doable. Exams were take home due to covid so that helped.

Great professor! His lectures can make me fall asleep sometimes but I enjoyed him! There are 11 homeworks 3 exams and the final is not cumulative! He also lets people work in groups of 2, 3 or working alone on homeworks.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Weekly homework comes from book- pretty easy. Gives review for exams but not the answers. Exams are pretty difficult compared to homework. I would recommend trying to complete the review questions and then going to office hours to go over them if you want to do good on exams. I made a 100 on every homework but still ended with a B because of exams.

He is a very nice prof and a fair grader, but his lectures aren't the easiest to follow. There's 3 things you need to do for an A: 1) watch Professor Leonard's lectures on youtube 2) go to office hours with the test review, it's just like the exam and he tells you how to solve it 3) go through the test with him, he almost always gives credit back
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures can be kind of boring but he is extremely helpful if you go to office hours. He gives a review that is very similar to the tests. Also just an overall nice guy

Professor Battle is not a bad teacher. His lectures are more based on the proof of the certain chapters. You dont have to show up to class, but because you have group homework once a week you need to turn it in. When it comes to test they are very easy if you know the review. The tests are exactly the same as the review.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Battle is not a good lecturer. The only way I did well in his class was by going to office hours 3-5 times a week. He is WAY more helpful in his office than in the classroom. His lectures can be hard to follow & he teaches information that isn't always relevant to what he will test. Do the suggested problems & go to office hours to do well.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His teaching can be boring, attendance is not mandatory. The book is okay, though his tests can be a bit tricky. If you see him during his office hours about questions you got wrong on the test, he might give you some points back.

Guy Battle is awesome; hes as old school as it gets when it comes to his lecture style. He has a great balance of being short and to the point but he never at the expense of full comprehension. Hes a great teacher in general, not exactly the most exciting guy in the world, but hell definitely prepare you for the tests and get you through class.

Battle is a dry but kind man. His research field is mathematical physics and so this is applied to a lot of his examples during the lecture. As someone who has already taken Cal 1 in high school, I found him confusing and could see it was just me by the class attendance. Not a terrible proff but there are definitely much better ones.

Really nice guy. Teaches it theory based. Never went to class & got an A bc it's Calculus. He is really nice but it was an 8 am so kinda rough. He goes off on random tangents and really enjoys proofs so if you're into that then go for battle

If you get Guy, don't drop the $100 for the textbook. You won't be using it. He is very, very intelligent, but doesn't explain concepts clearly at all. I took AP calculus AB in high school and was astounded at how weirdly he explained simple concepts. He doesn't have an online page (you can't check your grade) and won't work out examples in class.

Dr Battle is so smart you cannot understand what he is trying to teach. I was basically teaching myself by doing the homework. Also, none of his grades are online and you have to calculate them yourself.

Nice guy, but absolutely terrible in lecturing. Students either skip/work on HW during his class because of how hard it is to follow him. He goes into way more detail and depth than is required for any work in the course. So you're left to learn during lab from your TA or just study the textbook.

He is not a good teacher for simple aspects. As the semester went on, I understood more of what he said because he stopped assuming everyone knew exactly what he was saying. Also, he spends roughly 30% of class time trying to pick good numbers for examples instead of coming to class with examples already prepared to work out.
Dr. Battle gives a lot of definitions, and he often over complicates calculations, which makes them a lot harder to understand. He's not the worst, but not very easy to learn from.

If you have not taken calculus before, do not take him. You will be lost. I had taken calculus AB and BC before, which is the only reason why I got a B in this class. I did most of my learning outside of class. In the end, if you do the homework and fully understand it, you'll pass the class since the common exams aren't based on professors.

For those taking 151, do not take Dr. Battle. He has gotten good reviews for other subjects but calculus is not the one. I have taken BC calculus in high school and have done well in the class and the AP test, but despite taking calculus before I am struggling in his class. He overcomplicates things way too much and is very unclear and confused

I did all of my learning outside of the class. If I hadn't taken Calculus before his class I would of not done well. He does not explain things well at all but the overall tests for his class are not too difficult.

While Dr. Battle truly seems to enjoy and feel intrigued by math, his teaching is very hard to learn from. I learn more by reading the book than I do in his classes because he uses lots of terms and symbols (math short hand) without explaining. He doesn't explain the whys and hows for math, just works through equations to get to a shorter equation.

Guy is awesome! Easy class, sometimes he goes off on unrelated tangents. The textbook homework is confusing but if you know how to do the problems that he makes up you'll be fine on the tests. He gives a review for each exam which is really helpful. Final grade is made up of all the homeworks and the three tests
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Battle is super sweet, but definitely a little scatter-brained and gets flustered easily. The lecture before a test is really helpful because he tells you specifically what topics are covered and gives practice questions (but not the answers to them). The textbook helps a lot. Wish he would put notes or grades online. Tests are all FR, no MC.

Dr. Battle is very kind, and also extremely understanding whenever you have to talk to him about something you find difficult in his classes. He is a bit scatter-brained, so sometimes his lectures can get confusing when he talks about several things at once or makes a mistake on the board, but he is still definitely worth taking.

Dr. Battle is the sweetest professor. MATH 401 was not hard if you do/understand the homework because that is basically the tests. He gives you a review sheet for each test. If you want to know what hw problems he assigns, arrive early for class and actually go to class.
Professor Battle is the best professor I have ever met. He is kind, earnest very patient with student's questions.
good, nice

He definitely knows what he is talking about, but doesn't take the time to make it clear to the class or make the theorems connect to examples. I did most of my learning outside of class or based on knowledge I already knew from high school. Not recommended.
